learning.title: Bring up an ephemeral per-worktree stack instead of declaring an environment blocker
learning.trigger: A verification step needs the running API, worker, or PostgreSQL, and the shell has no root .env, the documented local database credentials fail, or the default Docker socket is permission-denied.
learning.mistake: Reported the fresh-stack browser smoke and one auth contract test as environment-blocked after one failed `psql` probe and a denied `/var/run/docker.sock`. The environment already provided a rootless container engine on a per-user socket, and infra/compose.yaml publishes every host port through an overridable variable, so the stack could have been created and torn down by the worktree itself.
learning.rule: Discover the container engine before concluding it is unavailable: try `docker version`, and when the default socket is denied inspect the user session (`systemctl --user cat <engine>.service`) for a rootless `--host=unix:///run/user/<uid>/<name>.sock` and set DOCKER_HOST to it. Give every worktree its own compose project with `--project-name bakery-<issue>-<short hash>` and free host ports through BAKERY_SERVER_PORT, BAKERY_INNGEST_PORT, and BAKERY_POSTGRES_PORT, start the whole stack with `up -d --wait`, run host processes against those published ports, and treat the stack as ephemeral: `down -v` the project when the work lands. Managing one stack per worktree is expected. Starting, stopping, removing, or reusing a compose project the worktree does not own is forbidden, as is publishing into a port another stack already holds.

verification.command: DOCKER_HOST=unix:///run/user/$(id -u)/formation-docker.sock docker compose --project-name bakery-124-<hash> -f infra/compose.yaml up -d --wait postgres redis inngest server worker
BAKERY_REAL_API=1 BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:<web port> pnpm --dir apps/web test:ui
DOCKER_HOST=unix:///run/user/$(id -u)/formation-docker.sock docker compose --project-name bakery-124-<hash> -f infra/compose.yaml down -v
verification.requirement: Record the compose project name, the published ports, the command that consumed them, and the teardown result. Leave no container, volume, or network behind, and never report a verification blocker while an owned stack can still be created.

learning.boundary: Missing shell variables are not evidence that the local environment is unavailable; see local-services-before-test-blocker. Ephemeral means created and destroyed by the worktree that needs it, not shared and not reused after merge.
